D.t: Everett Wess trails by 16.1 and wins 1% of simulations. Closing it takes about 138,216 voters switching sides, or 276,432 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +24.3 and R +8.0. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is R +14.5. Your best recent poll is Chism Strategies (D) at R +9.4; your worst is The Alabama Poll at R +21.2. 4 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Jefferson, a projected net 76,336 votes; Montgomery, a projected net 29,049 votes; Dallas, a projected net 5,958 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Madison, D +3.7, 8.5% of the vote; Mobile, R +2.0, 7.8% of the vote; Tuscaloosa, D +1.0, 3.9% of the vote; Talladega, R +11.2, 1.5% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Everett Wess runs furthest behind in Coffee, Cullman, Baldwin. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters without a degree, 68% of voters, 41 to 58, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.40 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 63% of voters, 41 to 58, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.17 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 61% of voters, 44 to 55, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.05 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Everett Wess: Immigration voters 14 to 85, White voters 30 to 69, Small counties 34 to 65. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$18K cash against $627K. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.3 points away from Everett Wess. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
Air cover: Outside groups spent $16.8M helping Barry Moore and $0 helping Everett Wess.

R.t: Barry Moore leads by 16.1 in the forecast and wins 99% of simulations. The cushion is about 276,432 votes; a one point swing is about 8,580 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +8.0 and R +24.3. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is R +14.5. Your best recent poll is The Alabama Poll at R +21.2; your worst is Chism Strategies (D) at R +9.4. 4 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Baldwin, a projected net 48,248 votes; Cullman, a projected net 24,164 votes; Shelby, a projected net 21,583 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Madison, D +3.7, 8.5% of the vote; Mobile, R +2.0, 7.8% of the vote; Tuscaloosa, D +1.0, 3.9% of the vote; Talladega, R +11.2, 1.5% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Barry Moore runs furthest behind in Talladega, Jefferson, Tuscaloosa. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters without a degree, 68% of voters, 58 to 41, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.40 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 63% of voters, 58 to 41, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.17 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 61% of voters, 55 to 44, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.05 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Barry Moore: Black voters 20 to 79, Independents 27 to 71, Moderates 38 to 60. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$627K cash against $18K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.

R.h: What the ballots so far say
